# EXPLORATORY SELF-INQUIRY — Paper 8 Self-Analysis (Task 1)
**Label: EXPLORATORY — not pre-registered, not confirmatory.**

## Seed Question
Paper 8 investigated whether explicit method operators (MOL) could reproduce persona effects in autonomous research loops. All five hypotheses were rejected. The primary findings were: (1) Operator framing acts as an epistemic precision regulator. (2) Stripped algorithmic context increases EME but increases false_proof_rate. (3) Structure and activation are separable epistemic variables. Analyze the epistemic trajectory of this paper's own argument. What are the dominant motifs? Where does the argument converge? What did the paper not explicitly look for but implicitly found?

## Dominant Motifs
- operator framing in self-directed learning systems / increases error rates
- operator framing in self-directed learning systems / decreases error rates
- operator framing in self-directed learning systems / increases generalization accuracy

## ClaimGraph Summary
1. [C001] (conf=0.48, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems influences error rates when applied to environments with limited semantic data
2. [C002] (conf=0.82, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems reduces error rates in environments with extremely sparse semantic data
3. [C003] (conf=0.42, disputed) operator framing in self-directed learning systems increases error rates when applied to environments with ambiguous but non-sparse semantic data
4. [C004] (conf=0.82, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems has no significant effect on error rates in environments with limited semantic data
5. [C005] (conf=0.85, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems increases generalization accuracy on out-of-distribution sparse semantic tasks
6. [C006] (conf=0.85, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems increases error rates in environments with extremely sparse semantic data
7. [C007] (conf=0.85, supported) operator framing that imposes premature structure in self-directed learning systems decreases error rates when applied to environments with ambiguous but non-sparse semantic data if the framing is dynamically updated via Bayesian priors

10. [B002] (conf=0.90, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems decreases error rates when applied to environments with ambiguous but non-sparse semantic data
11. [C011] (conf=0.85, supported) operator framing in self-directed learning systems significantly increases error rates in environments with limited semantic data when the system relies on externally sourced, static framing templates

## Attractor Structure
The claim trajectory shows a convergence around the core tension of operator framing increasing error rates in ambiguous but non-sparse semantic data environments. There is a persistent duality where operator framing both increases and decreases error rates under similar conditions, suggesting a complex interaction dependent on additional variables not fully explored.
